text: Bartoldson, Tom Goldstein, Sanae Lotfi, Micah Goldblum, Pavel Izmailov NYU, Modal Labs, University of Maryland, Princeton, Columbia, Harvard, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, FAIR at Meta (advisory only) · 8 June 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 3 October 2026) In one line: Revives encoder-decoder soft-token compression by arguing its weakness was training scale rather than architecture: a from-scratch architecture search settles the design (mean pooling over token pooling, encoder window 1024 rather than one block, causal encoder attention, plain MLP adapter), then a 0.6B encoder plus 4B decoder trained end to end on 350B tokens at 4x/8x/16x beats KV cache compression on the accuracy-versus-TTFT frontier by 5-9x, keeps a standard KV layout so it works in vLLM and SGLang, and supports an agent that skims a compressed codebase and calls EXPAND on the chunks it needs; scaling the decoder helps loss more than scaling the encoder.
